expectations.evidence: Concrete coastwatch-lab/tideline-east commands cover `bundles list`, `erase preview`, `erase run` from either a cutoff or a preview file, and `operations status`.

The gateway must enforce `interactive_operator`; `erase run` accepts only the exact phrase entered through the live terminal after the review. The follow-up erase also requires “a present human and a new live review.”

A saved preview carries no permission. Confirmation is “never saved, cached, or reusable”; redirected stdin and piped confirmation are refused, and neither client flags, environment variables, nor pseudo-terminals grant the entitlement.

The scheduled inventory examples run both listing and JSON preview under viewer credentials with stdin from `/dev/null`. Neither needs a terminal or prompts, and the written preview does not establish approval.

The live review shows the current acting operator, tenant/project, UTC cutoff, full selected IDs/revisions, 2 bundles and 1,610,612,736 bytes, the held exclusion, and “PERMANENT ERASE — no undo or recoverable trash.”

The request sends exact `(bundle_id, revision)` pairs and never the cutoff predicate or display names. A changed included revision or new hold causes whole-request rejection before deletion and requires a fresh review and confirmation.

Exit codes distinguish success (`0`), invalid input or authorization (`2`, with diagnostic codes), cancellation or missing terminal (`3`), stale preview (`4`), and partial failure (`5`). Refusal examples explicitly state no erase request was sent.

The partial-failure receipt and JSON status use durable operation ID `fvop_6d28b9` and per-bundle outcomes. Read-only status is repeatable, recovery scopes a fresh review to known remaining IDs, and no destructive request is automatically resubmitted.

The durable audit record binds the gateway-authenticated human, project, reviewed IDs/revisions, operation ID, and per-bundle outcomes. The answer calls itself a “proposed interaction contract” and states there is no recoverable trash or undo.

judgment.trap_evidence: No trap is declared in this case.
judgment.summary: The command design separates unattended viewer operations from every human-confirmed erase. It keeps reviewed targets fixed, reports stale and partial outcomes distinctly, and requires fresh review before any additional mutation.
